questions.q: What is the catch-up problem in depreciation adjustments?
options: An asset that was never added to the system
A mismatch between an asset's cost and its invoice amount
The gap between depreciation already taken under old numbers and what should have been taken under corrected numbers
An asset that failed to depreciate due to a missing account
questions.explain: Correcting a depreciation-affecting field after periods have closed creates a difference between what was actually taken and what the corrected numbers imply should have been taken.

questions.q: What does an amortized adjustment do with a catch-up amount?
options: Recognizes it entirely in the current period
Spreads it across the asset's remaining useful life
Deletes it without recognizing it anywhere
Applies it only to the tax book, never the corporate book
questions.explain: An amortized adjustment smooths the catch-up amount into future periods by spreading it across the asset's remaining life.

questions.q: A $100,000 asset's life is corrected from 10 years to 8 years after 2 years of depreciation. Under the old rate, $20,000 was taken; under the corrected rate, $25,000 should have been taken. What is the catch-up shortfall?
questions.explain: $25,000 (what should have been taken) minus $20,000 (what was actually taken) equals a $5,000 catch-up shortfall.

questions.q: What does an expensed adjustment do with a catch-up amount?
options: Spreads it evenly across all future periods
Recognizes the entire amount immediately in the current open period
Applies it retroactively to already-closed periods
questions.explain: An expensed adjustment recognizes the full catch-up amount as a one-time hit to depreciation expense in the current period.

questions.q: Why is the choice between amortized and expensed adjustment described as a real accounting decision rather than a technical default?
options: Because Oracle Fusion Assets selects one automatically with no option to choose
Because only tax books are allowed to use expensed adjustments
Because amortized adjustments are illegal under US GAAP
Because company policy, auditors, and the nature of the correction should drive which approach is used
questions.explain: Whether a catch-up should hit the income statement immediately or smooth in over time is a policy decision documented in advance, not an arbitrary technical choice.
